note: C14 (sustained aerobic flight) instantiated with the physiology chain's own numbers (physiology/, commit a1ca4f00), each cited by file and value. Every physiological input is a labelled PROXY from another teleost (the chain found no Exocoetidae physiology); the aerodynamic inputs are measured on the real fish (Park and Choi 2010). The lift-to-drag ratio committed is the measured maximum 4.37, which gives the LOWEST possible power required, so the elimination is a generous one; the physics thread's measured polar gives higher power at these speeds (1.42 W at 7 m/s for the flier). Units: cardiac_output in ml blood/s, arterial_O2_content in ml O2/ml blood, oxycaloric in J/ml O2, so eta x E x Q x Ca is in watts.

cardiac_output_ml_per_s.how: physiology/cardiac.js state(1): HR_max 153.01 bpm x SV_max 0.429 ml/kg = 65.64 ml/min/kg, x 0.06 kg / 60
cardiac_output_ml_per_s.source: durnford2026 Table 1 (Ucrit group), as cited in cardiac.js CARDIAC_PARAMS.warm

arterial_O2_content_ml_per_ml.how: physiology/haemoglobin.js content(15.8 kPa, {cap_ml_per_ml: 0.2062616}): Hill curve with P50 3.31 kPa and n 1.34 (trout, rummer2015) at the chain's reference arterial PO2 15.8 kPa (trout, mcarley2022; saturation 0.8905), warm-water capacity 0.2063 ml/ml tuned by physiology/index.js warmHbCapacity() from the snapper maximum blood O2 extraction 0.205 mg/ml (durnford2026); the chain's o2() reports arterialSat 0.8906 for the 0.06 kg fish
arterial_O2_content_ml_per_ml.source: rummer2015, mcarley2022, durnford2026 as cited in haemoglobin.js and index.js

muscular_efficiency.species: Salmo salar ventricular muscle (no fetched value for fish skeletal muscle)

oxycaloric_J_per_ml_O2.how: physiology/muscle.js MUSCLE_PARAMS.oxycalorific_J_per_mgO2 13.54 J/mg (gerry2014) divided by ML_O2_PER_MG 0.7 ml/mg (haemoglobin.js, standard constants)
oxycaloric_J_per_ml_O2.source: gerry2014 Fig. 1 legend as cited in muscle.js

aerobic_ceiling_W.how: eta x E x Q x Ca = 0.15 x 19.3429 x 0.0656413 x 0.1872334 (theorem: sustained_le)
aerobic_ceiling_W.note: the chain's own createPhysiology({mass_kg: 0.06}).powerAvailable() reports aerobic_W 0.00858 for work above the standard metabolic rate with the muscle caps applied; the theorem's ceiling is the gross figure and is larger, so the elimination below holds a fortiori

weight_N.source: physics/glide-data.csv, Park and Choi 2010 model L3, 0.06 kg x 9.81

lift_to_drag_max.source: physics/glide-data.csv, Park and Choi 2010 Table 2 (wind tunnel); the maximum, hence the most generous (lowest) power required

candidates.problem: Could the real flying fish sustain level flight on aerobic power (the question of physics test 4)?
candidates.description: Cypselurus hiraii specimen L3 (W 0.5886 N) claimed to sustain level lift-supported flight at the low end of the field airspeeds, 10 m/s, at its measured (L/D)max 4.37, with the physiology chain's cardiac output, arterial O2 content, efficiency and oxycaloric equivalent for a 0.06 kg fish in water (the generous case: in air the gills do not ventilate and the arterial content only falls).
candidates.source: physics/glide-data.csv (W, L/D, field speed); physiology/cardiac.js, haemoglobin.js, index.js, muscle.js at commit a1ca4f00 (see chain_inputs)

candidates.problem: Could the HYPOTHETICAL flier F1 sustain powered level flight at 7 m/s on aerobic power?
candidates.description: The physics thread's hypothetical flier F1 (same 0.06 kg body, enlarged fins) claimed to sustain level flight at 7 m/s at (L/D)max 4.37 with the same physiology chain, using the arterial O2 content at take-off (the generous bound: in air the gills do not ventilate and the store drains).
candidates.source: physics/flier/spec.json; physiology/ at commit a1ca4f00 (see chain_inputs); the physics polar gives P_req 1.42 W at 7 m/s, above the 0.94 W that (L/D)max 4.37 gives, so this is the generous case

candidates.problem: The same question at the minimum speed itself
candidates.description: Specimen L3 at its minimum lift-supported speed 9.85 m/s (the least power any lift-supported flight can need at (L/D)max), same physiology.
